messages.subject: Ordering stacked bar chart
parts:
I'm creating a stacked bar plot, but can't get ggplot2 to stack the bars in the order I want, even though I've set the factor levels of the stacking variable to the desired order. The data frame I'm using for plotting is called numCty and is pasted in below using dput. Here's my plotting code:

ggplot(numCty, aes(County, count, fill=Status)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", colour="black", lwd=0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label=count, y=pos), colour="grey30", size=2.4) +
  coord_flip() +
  xlab("County") + ylab("Number of Projects") +
  labs(fill="Project Status") +
  theme(axis.text=element_text(size=8),
        axis.title=element_text(size=9))

The plot looks exactly how I want it, with one exception: The ordering of the bars is currently (from left to right) green, blue, red (representing Status values of, respectively, Active, Inactive, and Completed). However, the ordering I want is red, green, blue (Status values of, respectively Completed, Active, Inactive).

As you can see in the numCty data frame pasted below, the factor levels of Status are in the order Completed, Active, Inactive, which (I would have thought) should result in ggplot stacking them in that order. Yet, ggplot is ignoring this ordering.

Thanks for any suggestions on how to get the desired ordering of the stacked bars.

Joel

numCty = structure(list(County = structure(c(19L, 19L, 19L, 1L, 2L, 15L,
10L, 10L, 10L, 18L, 18L, 18L, 11L, 11L, 11L, 16L, 16L, 20L, 20L,
20L, 12L, 17L, 17L, 17L, 13L, 3L, 14L, 4L, 21L, 21L, 21L, 5L,
6L, 7L, 9L, 8L), .Label = c("Butte", "Fresno", "San Joaquin",
"Santa Barbara", "Solano", "Stanislaus", "Tulare", "Yolo", "Ventura",
"Kern", "Merced", "Sacramento", "San Diego", "San Mateo", "Imperial",
"Monterey", "San Bernardino", "Los Angeles", "Alameda", "Orange",
"Santa Clara"), class = "factor"), Status = structure(c(2L, 3L,
1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 2L,
3L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L,
2L, 2L), .Label = c("Completed", "Active", "Inactive"), class = "factor"),
    count = c(7L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 4L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 6L, 1L, 1L,
    1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 4L, 4L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 3L,
    1L, 10L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 1L), pos = c(3.5, 7.5, 8.5,
    0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3, 6.5, 7.5, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 1,
    3, 0.5, 3, 7, 1.5, 1.5, 3.5, 4.5, 1.5, 0.5, 1.5, 0.5, 5,
    11.5, 14.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 0.5)), .Names = c("County",
"Status", "count", "pos"), row.names = c(NA, -36L), class = "data.frame")

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Ordering stacked bar chart
parts:
You'll need to sort the data frame first:

numCty <- numCty[order(numCty$County, numCty$Status),]

...after which things plot correctly, except those geom_text labels, which are now out of position. You may want to compute them programatically, something like:

# assumes a sorted data frame
runningsum <- 0
for(i in 2:nrow(numCty)) {
     runningsum <- ifelse(numCty[i,"County"] == numCty[i-1,"County"], runningsum+numCty[i-1,"count"], 0)
     numCty[i,"pos"] <- runningsum + numCty[i,"count"]/2
}
numCty[1,"pos"] <- numCty[1,"count"]/2


Ben

On Sunday, November 30, 2014 8:20:22 PM UTC-8, eipi10 wrote:

I'm creating a stacked bar plot, but can't get ggplot2 to stack the bars in the order I want, even though I've set the factor levels of the stacking variable to the desired order. The data frame I'm using for plotting is called numCty and is pasted in below using dput. Here's my plotting code:

ggplot(numCty, aes(County, count, fill=Status)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", colour="black", lwd=0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label=count, y=pos), colour="grey30", size=2.4) +
  coord_flip() +
  xlab("County") + ylab("Number of Projects") +
  labs(fill="Project Status") +
  theme(axis.text=element_text(size=8),
        axis.title=element_text(size=9))

Based on following example

 

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/25512656/ggplot2-stacked-bar-not-ordering-by-manually-defined-factor-order?rq=1

 

It seems if you put “order=Status” in your code, you can order the bars in ordering red, green, blue.

 

ggplot(numCty, aes(County, count, fill=Status, order=Status)) +

geom_bar(stat="identity", colour="black", lwd=0.2) +

  geom_text(aes(label=count, y=pos), colour="grey30", size=2.4) +

  coord_flip() +

  xlab("County") + ylab("Number of Projects") +

  labs(fill="Project Status") +

  theme(axis.text=element_text(size=8),

        axis.title=element_text(size=9))

the only thing mass up is the labels for each stack, you may have to fix the pos to label each stack correctly.

 

David
